title: Limits and continuity
goal: Check whether a graph can be drawn without lifting your pen (continuity), and glue piecewise formulas together smoothly by matching their heights at the seam.

beforeThis.skill: Quick check: a formula only breaks where you divide by $0$, take an even root of a negative number, take $\ln(\le 0)$, or jump between two pieces.

seeIt.title: Continuity & Types of Discontinuities
seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Pictures removable holes, jumps, and vertical asymptotes alongside the Intermediate Value Theorem (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n3G1L3yqPI0).

questions.asking: Think of a periodic function with a denominator that hits $0$ over and over again (like $\tan x$ or $1/\sin x$).
questions.statement: Give an example of a function (you can write a formula, or sketch a graph) that has infinitely many infinite discontinuities.

questions.asking: Check if knowing both $\lim_{t \to 5} f(t) = 17$ and that $f$ is continuous at $t = 5$ guarantees $f(5) = 17$.
questions.statement: Suppose $\lim_{t \to 5} f(t) = 17$, and suppose $f(t)$ is continuous at $t = 5$. True or false: $f(5) = 17$.

questions.asking: Check if knowing $\lim_{t \to 5} f(t) = 17$ without knowing continuity is enough to guarantee $f(5) = 17$.
Find the number $k$ that makes the value $a(0)$ match the limit of $a(x)$ as $x$ approaches $0$.
questions.statement:
Find a constant $k$ so that the function

$$a(x) = \begin{cases} x \sin\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) & \text{when } x \ne 0 \\[6pt] k & \text{when } x = 0 \end{cases}$$

is continuous at $x = 0$.

questions.asking: Find every real number $x$ where the formula can be plugged in safely without dividing by $0$ or taking an invalid root/log.
questions.statement: Describe all points for which this function is continuous: $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}$.

questions.asking: List all inputs $x$ where the formula works without dividing by $0$ or putting a negative number inside a square root.
questions.statement: Describe all points for which this function is continuous: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \cos(x)}}$.

questions.asking: Since $1/\sin x$ only breaks when you divide by $0$, exclude every angle $x$ where $\sin x = 0$ (multiples of $\pi$).
questions.statement: Describe all points for which this function is continuous: $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sin x}$.

questions.asking: Find every real number $c$ where the two branches of $f(x)$ meet continuously at $x = c$, and write out the limit justification.
questions.statement:
Find all values of $c$ such that the following function is continuous at $x = c$:

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} 8 - cx & \text{if } x \le c \\ x^2 & \text{if } x > c \end{cases}$$

Use the definition of continuity to justify your answer.

questions.asking: Find every constant $c$ for which the two branches of $f(x)$ connect continuously at $x = 0$, and justify using one-sided limits.
questions.statement:
Find all values of $c$ such that the following function is continuous everywhere:

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2 + c & x \ge 0 \\ \cos(cx) & x < 0 \end{cases}$$

Use the definition of continuity to justify your answer.

questions.asking: Find all values of $c$ that make the two branches of $f(x)$ match at the transition point $x = 2c$, and justify using the definition of continuity.
questions.statement:
Find all values of $c$ such that the following function is continuous:

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} 6 - cx & \text{if } x \le 2c \\ x^2 & \text{if } x > 2c \end{cases}$$

Use the definition of continuity to justify your answer.
